operations.specification:
This operation registers a new todo user account in the system, associated with the actor table 'todo_users'. The purpose of this API is to allow an individual to create a new user profile that will be able to securely access, create, and manage their own todo items. The endpoint accepts necessary registration fields (as defined by the 'todo_users' schema) such as a username and password, and creates a new user record.

Upon successful registration, the system issues a JWT-based access token and refresh token, enabling authenticated sessions for the user. Registration enforces validation and uniqueness constraints as described in the 'todo_users' schema comments (for example, unique username and strong password requirements). This is a public endpoint and does not require prior authentication.

Security of the registration process is ensured by validating all input fields and following best practices for password storage (i.e., salted hashes as described in schema or project config). Any violation of registration rules, such as attempting to register with a duplicate username, results in informative error messages.

Registration is the foundational step in the user authentication workflow and is required before performing any other user-authenticated actions. This endpoint is typically used prior to the login operation.

Integration: A successful join/register response contains authorization tokens in the response body of type ITodoUser.IAuthorized, as per service prefix and naming convention.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables a new todo user to register for personal access to the service, directly creating a record in the 'todo_users' table. All fields required for account creation, such as username and password, are validated against the schema constraints. Uniqueness of username is enforced at the database level according to comments on 'todo_users.username'.

The join process is critical for user onboarding, as described in the requirements. Upon successful registration, the system issues a JWT-based access token and refresh token, following the platform's authentication policy. No authentication or prior session is needed to call this endpoint.

Business context: The registering todo user establishes a secure identity in the application, enabling secure ownership of todo items and associations with their sessions in 'todo_user_sessions'.

Security practices such as email verification or password constraints are enforced according to project requirements documented in analysis files and the 'todo_users' schema. Detailed error reporting is provided for failed registration attempts.

This operation is closely related to the user login and token refresh operations, serving as the initial entry point to the authentication workflow for 'user' actors.
operations.summary: Register a new todo user in todo_users table and issue initial JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: The required registration data for a new todo user, as defined by ITodoUser.ICreate schema (matches fields in todo_users table needed for account creation).

responseBody.description: The authentication tokens and authorized user info issued upon successful registration. Matches ITodoUser.IAuthorized DTO structure.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
This operation logs in an existing todo user, authenticating credentials against the actor table 'todo_users'. The endpoint expects a login request containing required authentication fields (such as username and password) as defined by the schema.

The login process validates user credentials and, upon success, issues a JWT-based access and refresh token according to the service’s authentication policies. This enables the user to maintain authenticated sessions and access their personal todo data securely.

Credential validation strictly follows the rules documented in the 'todo_users' schema, such as password verification and account existence checks. Security is a priority, using best practices described in the schema comments (e.g., password hashing, brute force protection if specified).

The login endpoint is essential for users to initiate an authenticated session after registering or for returning users. Upon successful login, tokens are returned using ITodoUser.IAuthorized response type.

If login fails due to incorrect credentials or account issues, the endpoint provides appropriate error messages, ensuring the API’s behavior is transparent and informative.

This operation is tightly coupled with the registration (join) and refresh token operations, forming the core user authentication workflow.
operations.description:
Authenticate an existing todo user via credentials stored in the 'todo_users' schema. The endpoint validates the username and password exactly as described in schema comments or requirements for secure authentication.

Upon successful authentication, a new JWT-based access token and refresh token are generated and returned to the user in the ITodoUser.IAuthorized DTO structure. Failed login attempts (e.g., invalid credentials) result in standard error responses following error handling policy.

This operation implements the core authentication logic needed for a user to access the todo API securely. It is publicly accessible but enforces strict validation for login data.

Business context: Successful login links the authenticated user to their personal todo data through 'todo_user_sessions', as described in business requirements.

Closely related operations: user registration (join) and token refresh, which together provide full authentication capability for the 'user' actor.
operations.summary: Authenticate todo user in todo_users table and issue new JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Login credentials corresponding to a user in todo_users. Defined by ITodoUser.ILogin DTO (must match schema fields for credential authentication).

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and authorized user info provided on successful login. Uses ITodoUser.IAuthorized response DTO.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
This operation refreshes expiring JWT tokens for an authenticated todo user, referencing user and session tables 'todo_users' and 'todo_user_sessions'. It allows a valid refresh token from a previously authenticated session to generate new access and refresh tokens in accordance with authentication standards detailed in requirements and schema comments.

The refresh process validates the provided refresh token against the session records for the user, ensuring that only active and legitimate sessions can acquire new tokens. Token issuance policies and expiration handling are closely linked to the system configuration and security practices.

Security measures include invalidating refresh tokens on sign-out or excessive failures, and returning errors for invalid or expired tokens as described in system requirements. All new tokens are delivered using the ITodoUser.IAuthorized response structure.

The token refresh endpoint is not public: it requires a valid refresh token. This enforces secure continuity of user sessions between explicit logins.

This operation is central to the lifecycle of authenticated sessions, complimenting the login and registration endpoints by allowing clients to sustain authenticated access without continual credential re-entry.
operations.description:
Refresh JWT tokens for a todo user, validating the provided refresh token according to session records in 'todo_user_sessions' schema.

This endpoint is accessible only with a valid refresh token, and returns new access and refresh tokens as specified in schema and requirements. Security policies on refreshing and revoking tokens are enforced as described in the service configuration.

Business context: Token refresh links authenticated clients to their ongoing user sessions and allows seamless access to todo data.

Closely related endpoints: user login (issue tokens with credentials) and registration (initial join and token provisioning). Together, these endpoints enable a secure, session-based authentication workflow for todo users.

Error conditions such as expired, revoked, or invalid tokens are handled precisely as documented in error-handling requirements and schema comments.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT authentication tokens for todo user using a valid refresh token.

requestBody.description: Refresh token data as required for the session, matching ITodoUser.IRefresh DTO definition.

responseBody.description: Newly issued authentication tokens and user info after successful refresh. Data shape defined by ITodoUser.IAuthorized DTO.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves profile details of the currently authenticated user. It is mapped to the todo_users table and returns personal information for the requester only. This endpoint is essential for user experience, enabling applications to display account metadata, email, and audit timestamps in a privacy-safe manner. The operation enforces strict self-access using authentication context and does not require explicit path parameters or a request body.
operations.description:
Retrieve the profile and metadata for the currently authenticated user in the Todo List application.

This operation uses the authentication context to identify the user making the request. It returns the user's unique email, registration and last update timestamps, but omits password information and any administrative fields to comply with privacy requirements.

As the application supports only personal todo management, no roles or group-level data are ever exposed. The endpoint is secured for self-use only, meaning users cannot retrieve profiles for other users. Related operations include updating credentials (handled elsewhere) and managing session information.

Errors occur if the requester is unauthenticated or if the underlying user record cannot be found, for example if the account was deleted after login.
operations.summary: Retrieve the authenticated user profile from the todo_users table

responseBody.description: Full profile and account metadata for the authenticated user.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of active and historical session records for the authenticated user. It operates on the todo_user_sessions table, filtering sessions based on the self-authenticated user context. The endpoint is intended for managing and auditing personal device and browser logins, providing presence, history, and context for each session, such as IP address, login URI, and timestamps. Input supports search, pagination, and sorting for session records owned strictly by the authenticated user.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and optionally filtered list of all current and past session records for the authenticated user.

The list can be filtered by connection time, expiration, and device/browser context, and supports searching for session context details, including IP, URL, and referrer. The returned data only includes sessions owned by the currently authenticated user, enforcing strict privacy and ownership. This operation is essential for security awareness and enables users to review and manage device/browser logins.

If provided, pagination and sorting parameters enable clients to efficiently browse large session histories. Security errors are raised if the requester is unauthenticated. The response always omits any information about other users' sessions for privacy compliance.
operations.summary: List all sessions for the authenticated user from the todo_user_sessions table

requestBody.description: Optional search, pagination, and filter parameters for user session listing.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of session details for the authenticated user.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the details of an authenticated user's own session, given a specific session ID. It operates on the todo_user_sessions table, which tracks active and historical login sessions for a personal todo user. Each session is strictly linked to a single user via the foreign key todo_user_id. This endpoint provides users with insight into their session activity, including audit data like IP address, origin URL, referrer, start, and expiration time. The path parameter sessionId refers to the unique session identifier (UUID) as defined in the database model. Only the authenticated user (actor: user) may access their session, with access restrictions enforced to ensure privacy and compliance with business rules.
operations.summary: Retrieve authenticated user's own session by sessionId from todo_user_sessions.
operations.description:
This API operation allows an authenticated user to fetch the details of a specific login session belonging to their own account. The sessionId path parameter must reference a valid session record which is both owned by the requesting user and exists in the todo_user_sessions table.

Only the session data for the current user is accessible—attempting to query a session owned by another user will result in a clear access-denied error, as mandated by strict privacy requirements. The payload includes all session audit and context fields (IP, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at), making this endpoint essential for session management and user transparency.

Security is enforced via both path checking (me = current user context) and foreign key validation. This endpoint does not permit the creation, update, or deletion of sessions—administrative modification is intentionally excluded to comply with requirements that sessions are managed exclusively via authentication flows.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the login session to be viewed. Must belong to the current authenticated user and exist in todo_user_sessions.

responseBody.description: Complete session information for the specified session, if owned by the current user. Includes all audit fields and metadata from todo_user_sessions.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation queries and retrieves a filtered, paginated list of the authenticated user's own todo items. It operates on the todo_todos table, which links each todo to its owning user through user_id. The operation supports advanced searching, filtering, sorting, and paging by all primary business fields—status (is_completed), due date, priority, creation date, and full-text search on title or description via GIN indexes. Only the user's own records are visible or queryable. The endpoint enforces application-level unique constraints and supports business rule-compliant response formats.
operations.summary: Search, filter, and paginate the authenticated user's own todos using advanced criteria from todo_todos.
operations.description:
This API operation provides a paginated list of personal todo items for the authenticated user, supporting business rule-driven filtering, sorting, and searching. The operation accepts a complex search/filter request body aligned with ITodoTodo.IRequest, which allows filtering by completion status, due date, priority (restricted to 'low', 'medium', or 'high'), and full-text search on both the title and the description fields.

Only the requesting user's own todos are included in the result set, ensuring privacy per requirements. The response contains paginated summary information for each todo, including metadata such as creation/update timestamps, status, and all custom fields visible to the user (from todo_todos). Pagination and sorting follow standard conventions to support efficient list views in the UI.

This endpoint does not expose any information from other users' todos, ensuring strict business and security rules are upheld. All filtering and sorting are performed server-side for performance and data security.

requestBody.description: Advanced search, filter, sorting, and paging options for querying user's own todos. Refer to ITodoTodo.IRequest for available request fields.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the authenticated user's todos matching the search and filter criteria; each item summarized per list display requirements, based on todo_todos.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detail of a single todo item belonging to the authenticated user. It uses the todo_todos table as defined in the Prisma schema, which represents individual todo items scoped strictly to their owning user for privacy and multi-tenancy. The operation expects a todoId parameter referencing the unique identifier for the target todo. It returns the complete todo record, including relevant metadata (created_at, updated_at, completed_at) and business fields (title, description, due_date, priority, and completion status). The operation validates that the user has access rights to the specified todo (ownership enforced by user_id) and that the todo exists. It does not expose data across user boundaries.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single todo item by its unique identifier for the authenticated user.

This endpoint allows users to view the details of an individual todo, including title, description, due date, priority, completion status, and all associated timestamps. All data returned is strictly limited to the requesting user's own todos; access to other users' todos is not permitted under business privacy rules.

Security checks are enforced, verifying that the todoId provided belongs to the currently authenticated user in the system. Attempts to access another user's todo will result in a not found or forbidden response. The operation references the todo_todos table from the database schema and covers all base fields as documented. Error handling includes missing or invalid identifiers and unauthorized access attempts.

Related operations include creating a new todo (POST /todos) and searching a user's todos (PATCH /todos).
operations.summary: Retrieve a single todo item (todo_todos) by ID for the authenticated user.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the todo item. Must belong to the authenticated user.

responseBody.description: Detailed information of the requested todo item, including all fields defined in the todo_todos schema.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A todo item must first be created before it can be retrieved by its ID. Creating a todo provides the valid todoId required to successfully call the GET endpoint.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item for the authenticated user and stores it in the todo_todos table, which is the main entity for managing individual todos. The required attributes are: title (max 255 chars per schema), and optional fields include description, due_date, priority (enum: low, medium, high), and the completion status defaults to false. Ownership is strictly enforced: user_id is always derived from the authenticated session and cannot be overridden by client payloads. Application logic validates for duplicate title/due date per user (as required by the business rule unique index). Timestamps for creation and update are automatically set. Deletion is irreversible; completed_at is only populated if is_completed is true. The response returns the created todo including all metadata.
operations.description:
Create a new personal todo item for the authenticated user.

This API endpoint allows users to add a task to their private list, specifying a required title along with optional details such as description, due date, and priority. Upon creation, the todo is linked to the user's account (user_id is assigned server-side) and marked incomplete by default.

Business rules enforce uniqueness of title and due date per user to avoid accidental duplicate entries, as defined by the unique index in the schema. Security is enforced by bypassing any external user_id in the request body; only the session's user is honored. On success, the API returns the complete todo record as persisted in the database, including all audit fields and associations. The operation aligns with the todo_todos database schema and respects all privacy boundaries.
operations.summary: Create a new todo_todos record for the authenticated user with title and optional details.

requestBody.description: Details for creating a new todo item: title (required), and optional description, due_date, priority.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo record, including server-generated fields and all schema-defined business data.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates all editable fields of a particular todo item in the todo_todos table. The todo is identified by its unique ID path parameter and must belong to the authenticated user. Updatable fields include title, description, due date, priority, and completion status; business logic enforces uniqueness of title and due date per user, and restricts operations to the item's owner. Both created_at and updated_at are managed automatically. The operation fully complies with strict privacy and one-user-per-todo business requirements from the underlying schema.
operations.description:
Update a user's personal todo item with new attributes.

The operation allows an authenticated user to modify the title, description, due date, priority, and completion status of a todo item they own. Updates are subject to business validation rules from the Prisma schema, including unique constraints on title and due date per user, preservation of task privacy, and correct handling of date and priority fields as described in the schema comments.

Authentication is required; only the owning user can update their todos. Attempts to update a todo owned by another user result in access denial. The system automatically manages audit fields for tracking changes.

Clients are expected to send only modifiable fields in the request body, using the ITodoTodo.IUpdate type. In case of conflict with validation rules or ownership, detailed error messages are returned. This operation centers on direct user-driven management of their todo list, with robust schema-driven protections against data leakage or integrity violation.
operations.summary: Update a specific todo item in the todo_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a todo item.

requestBody.description: Fields to update for the specified todo. Follows schema validations and uniqueness constraints per user.

responseBody.description: Updated todo item with latest attributes and audit fields.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a user's specific todo item from the todo_todos table. The target is identified via its unique ID in the path. The operation only succeeds if the todo belongs to the authenticated user. Deletion is irreversible—there is no soft delete per the schema and business requirements—so all data and references are immediately removed from the system. Audit concerns are satisfied with retained logs elsewhere outside the todo_todos table.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a personal todo item from the authenticated user's list.

This operation enforces strict ownership validation: only the owner of a todo may delete it, as verified by the user_id foreign key. No soft deletion is performed—deleted records are gone permanently in accordance with the schema's business rules and design comments. This supports a privacy-first model in which each user's todos are fully private and isolated.

The delete is final and does not affect any shared or public data, as todos are never shared. Operations track access, validate user ownership, and fail with appropriate messages for unauthorized attempts. Users must exercise caution when invoking this endpoint, given the irreversible nature of the operation. The response confirms the deleted todo item data immediately before deletion.
operations.summary: Permanently delete a user's specific todo item from the todo_todos table.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for a todo item.

responseBody.description: Details of the todo item as it existed before deletion.

operations.name: erase

Total pages.

Equal to {@link records} / {@link limit} with ceiling.

JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

ITodoUser.ICreate.description:
Request body schema for registering a new todo user in the system. Corresponds to the creation of a record in the 'todo_users' table and enforces unique, secure user authentication. This schema accepts all and only the fields required for user self-registration, deferring identity context and system-managed fields to the backend. Registration is the foundational entry for todo system authentication workflows.

The schema includes required fields for account creation according to the database schema: a unique email and a password (plain text for validation and hashing, never a hash). It enforces business logic documented in the schema comments—such as uniqueness and required validation rules for the email field. System-managed information like IDs or timestamps, and authentication context fields are not included. Password security, uniqueness, and field validation are described in the provider's security requirements.

Business context: After submission, the backend will create a secure user record, hash the password, and issue an authentication token.

email.description: User's email address for authentication. Must be unique across all users. This field is required for account creation and subsequent login. Must be a valid RFC 5322 email address per schema comments and API requirements.

password.description: User's account password (plain text, will be hashed on the backend). Minimum length 8 characters. Should not be stored or logged in plain text. Must satisfy password policy from requirements.

href.description: Current connection URL (the client page from which the registration was made). Used for audit and security context tracking. Required for self-registration by the actor.

referrer.description: Referrer URL captured at the time of registration. Provides context around the user journey leading to registration. Required for session context.

ip.description: Optional client IP address. Can be null if not provided by client. Used for session audit and fraud detection. The server may also extract this. Not required, but included for SSR and audit scenarios.

ITodoUser.IAuthorized.description:
Response body schema for authenticated todo user after registration, login, or token refresh. Delivers the JWT tokens and essential authorized user context as required for authenticated API communication. Used as the return type for both join and login flows (and refresh).

This schema delivers a newly issued JWT token and refresh token as a nested IAuthorizationToken reference, along with the basic identifying context for the authorized user. Tokens enable continued authenticated access and association with the underlying todo user records. This type is atomic for authentication—contains only what the client and server need post-authentication (no password field).

Fulfills atomicity for authentication responses, ensuring clients receive all information needed to establish or refresh an authenticated session.

id.description: Unique identifier for the authorized todo user. Maps to todo_users.id in the database. Identifies the principal for all future client activity.

email.description: Email address used for account authentication and identifier. Must be unique across all users. Serves as the login principal and for password resets.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created (UTC). Used for audit and business reporting.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last change to this user account (credentials, metadata, etc.). Allows business auditing and security checks.

ITodoUser.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for the todo user authentication flow.

Contains the fields required for credential verification against the 'todo_users' table, supporting secure login via email and password as described in requirements.

Session context fields (href and referrer) are required to comply with audit, security, and session management, enabling tracing of login activity per business rules. IP is optional and, if absent, should be captured from the connection by the backend.

Never include password hashes or non-plain secrets; clients MUST only submit plain passwords, which are hashed server-side. See security rules.

email.description: User's unique email address for authentication. Must match an email in the 'todo_users' database table. Used as the login identifier.

password.description: Plain user password to be authenticated. NEVER hashed in the request. Backend will verify this against the stored password_hash.

oneOf.description: Client IP address for audit logging and context tracking. Useful for tracing suspicious login activity. Optional: backend will supply if the frontend omits.

ip.description: Client IP address for audit logging and context tracking. Useful for tracing suspicious login activity. Optional: backend will supply if the frontend omits.

href.description: URL that the client was visiting at time of login. Required for proper session and audit trail. Used for UX/analytics.

referrer.description: The referring URL provided by the browser/client when login was triggered. Required for session context and audit purpose.

ITodoUser.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token request for authenticated todo users.

Used to obtain new authentication tokens (JWT) by presenting a valid refresh token issued during a prior login. Ensures continued access while maintaining security as defined in requirements and session schema rules. Structure is minimal, only requiring the token for renewal.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token string previously issued to the user via ITodoUser.IAuthorized. Required to validate and issue new access/refresh tokens.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for the user. Assigned upon account creation and used for authentication and entity relations.

email.description: Email address used for account authentication and identifier. Must be unique across all users. Serves as the login principal and for password resets.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user account was created (UTC). Used for audit and business reporting.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last change to this user account (credentials, metadata, etc.). Allows business auditing and security checks.

ITodoUser.description:
User accounts for personal todo management.

Represents an authenticated user of the Todo List application. Each user has a unique email and a securely set password (never exposed by this schema). The profile exposes account metadata only for the authenticated user, strictly omitting any role, group, or administrative fields. This guarantees privacy and ensures only account holders can access this information. Timestamps support UX and audit logging. All user management operations refer to this type.

ITodoUserSession.description: Session record for a user's authenticated login, supporting device/session management, history, and security. Directly maps to the todo_user_sessions Prisma table.

id.description: Session unique identifier (UUID). Primary key for session tracking and lookup.

todo_user_id.description: Reference to the owning user account. Foreign key to the todo_users table.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was created. Used for security audits and unusual activity detection.

href.description: Origin URL at the time of session creation, useful for tracking entry point and client context for the session.

referrer.description: Referrer URL provided at login — typically the previous page or inbound source at time of authentication.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp when the session was established. Used for session activity metrics and audit logging.

expired_at.description: Timestamp at which the session expired, was terminated, or logged out. Null indicates an active session.

page.description: Pagination page number. Sets which batch of session results to retrieve. Optional; defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum results per page. Optional; defaults to a system value (usually 20 or 50).

search.description: Case-insensitive string for searching IP, href, or referrer context data across all the user's sessions. Optional.

oneOf.description: Field to sort session results by. Defaults to created_at if not specified.
Field to sort session results by. Defaults to created_at if not specified.

order_by.description: Field to sort session results by. Defaults to created_at if not specified.

ITodoUserSession.IRequest.description:
Parameters for searching and paginating the current user's session history.

Supports full session context exploration, security audits, and device/browser management. No user_id parameter is ever present: filtering is always done contextually for the authenticated user.

ITodoTodo.IRequest.description: Query request structure for a user's own todo list supporting filtering, searching, sorting, and pagination. All filters are optional but combining multiple enables flexible business logic-aligned queries.

page.description: Pagination: The page number to retrieve (1-based). Default is 1 if omitted.

limit.description: Pagination: Number of todos per page. Default may be 20; hard maximum is 100 per requirements.

is_completed.description: Status filter: true to include only completed todos, false for incomplete, omitted for both. Also supports null for both.

due_date_from.description: If set, only return todos with due_date on or after this date (ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD). Null/omitted means no lower bound.

due_date_to.description: If set, only return todos with due_date on or before this date (ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD). Null/omitted means no upper bound.

priority.description: Priority filter – restrict to a specific priority ('low', 'medium', or 'high'). Null/omitted means no priority filter.

search.description: Full-text search string; case-insensitive matches on title and description. Optional.

oneOf.description: Sort field: which field to sort results by (created_at, due_date, or priority).

Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Sort direction: 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

ITodoTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for todo items, used in lists or compact displays. Selects a minimal set of fields for performance and clarity, omitting detailed description and audit data unless essential for display.

Shows identification, owner, key task attributes, and status. Intended for list endpoints and contexts where full entity details are not necessary. Follows all privacy and unique-per-user business constraints from the main schema.

ITodoTodo.description:
Represents an individual todo item in the user's personal list. Each todo is strictly owned by one authenticated user and contains task-related information with metadata for audit and privacy. Tasks are private and never shared across users.

Main properties include a required title, optional description, optional due date, optional priority (with allowed values: 'low', 'medium', 'high'), a boolean completion status, and a timestamp marking completion if completed. Unique per-user constraints apply to the (title, due_date) tuple. System-managed audit fields help recovery and tracking, and deletion is irreversible.

Used as the primary entity in todo CRUD operations, API responses, and user-specific filtering. DTO strictly follows database and privacy rules.

ITodoTodo.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new todo item as the authenticated user.

Clients provide the title. Optionally, they may include a description, a due date (ISO 8601), and a priority ('low', 'medium', 'high'). All fields are validated per the schema. Business logic enforces a unique title and due date for each user and automatically associates ownership with the authenticated session (user_id from auth context). Completion state defaults to false; completed_at is managed by business logic. This schema is used for POST /todo/user/todos.

Ownership, timestamps, and user_id are server-managed and never accepted from the client. Irreversible deletion applies to all created todos.

ITodoTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO to update a user's todo item. Allows modification of all editable fields under business and validation rules from the database schema. Restricted to the owning authenticated user—neither id nor user_id is updatable by the client.

Editable properties include title, description, due_date, priority, completion status, and optional completion timestamp. Business logic enforces uniqueness constraints and type validation. All properties are optional, and only those sent will be updated. Ownership and audit fields are system managed and cannot be modified via this DTO. Intended exclusively for authenticated users updating their own todos.
